title: Concurrent eviction rollback caused sticky-prefetch amplification during tenant bursts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: During a high-throughput customer load test (simulating peak tail requests) the KV cache experienced a coordinated failure mode where concurrent eviction rollbacks combined with an aggressive async prefetch change caused repeated re-insertions of large prefix entries. This produced tenant-scoped memory amplification and degraded allocator throughput, resulting in elevated OOM/eviction storms on several Dedicated hosts. This ticket collects incident follow-ups, short-term mitigations, and a staged long-term roadmap to prevent recurrence.
impact: High: 8 Dedicated hosts entered degraded state, several production tenants observed increased tail latencies and elevated token cost due to rework. No user data loss; service degradations lasted up to 27 minutes for impacted host pool during the event window.
timeline: 2026-02-27 14:12 UTC: Load spike begins (internal soak). 14:18 UTC: Alerts for memory pressure and KV eviction rate increase. 14:22 UTC: First host OOM and restart; automated autoscale triggered. 14:25 UTC: Observed repeating insert+evict cycles correlated with async prefetch RPC latency spikes. 14:30 UTC: Emergency mitigation: temporarily disabled aggressive async prefetch for the affected pool (rollout 14:32). 14:39 UTC: memory pressure subsided; 14:45 UTC: gradual confirmation of stabilization and post-incident monitoring. 15:00 UTC: Incident declared resolved for primary hosts; follow-up planning initiated.
root_cause_summary: A recent prefetch heuristic change (PR: github.com/redwood/serve/pull/2428) made async prefetch aggressively fetch full prefixes on cold misses and retry on transient backend latency. When combined with a bug in the eviction rollback path (race on slab metadata), the system could repeatedly evict and reinsert the same large prefix entry under concurrent contention. This created a hot-loop where tenant allocation grew faster than eviction could reclaim due to rollback churn, amplifying memory usage and causing allocator stalls.
immediate_mitigations_completed: 1) Reverted aggressive async prefetch heuristic (rolled back config and gated behind feature flag). 2) Applied temporary throttle on prefetch retries to 1 per-prefix-per-5s per-tenant. 3) Raised eviction backoff timer and enabled additional logging for rollback paths. 4) Temporarily increased heap safety margin on Dedicated pool to absorb residual churn.
follow_up_tasks: Patch eviction rollback race: add atomic metadata update and linearize allocator interactions (owner: Jonah Miller, estimate: 5) - due 2026-03-24
Rework prefetch policy: change from aggressive full-prefix fetch to staged prefix streaming with size cap and backoff (owner: Priya Desai, estimate: 8) - due 2026-04-07
Add tenant-scoped prefetch token-bucket to limit burst amplification (owner: Sasha Nguyen, estimate: 3) - due 2026-03-31
Add integration test that simulates concurrent evict/reinsert churn and validates memory boundedness (owner: Eng QA, estimate: 5) - due 2026-03-20

Extend eviction telemetry: emit per-tenant eviction/reinsert counters, rollback counts, slab contention metrics, and histograms for prefetch retry latency (owner: Observability team, estimate: 5) - due 2026-03-17

Canary rollout plan: stage fixes to a single Dedicated host pool, run 48h soak with synthetic burst traffic and Chaos injection of persistent prefetch latency (owner: SRE, estimate: 2) - due 2026-04-10
Update runbook: add detection rules for 'evict-reinsert oscillation', automatic mitigation (disable prefetch) and post-restart hygiene (owner: SRE Runbooks, estimate: 1) - due 2026-03-15
Post-release retrospective: schedule cross-team blameless review and review of release gating for prefetch heuristics (owner: Aisha Kapoor, estimate: 1) - due 2026-04-15
